title.narrative: Strengthening Freedom of Expression and Safety of Journalists in Afghanistan

description.narrative:
Introduction: Journalists in Afghanistan operate under severe constraints, facing threats to their safety and restrictions on freedom of expression. This workplan focuses specifically on strengthening these areas by leveraging key international advocacy moments: World Press Freedom Day, International Day for Universal Access to Information, and International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists to raise awareness, mobilize stakeholders, and promote accountability. Objectives:
1. Use UN observance days to amplify awareness on journalist safety and freedom of expression. 2. Advocate for accountability and access to information through targeted campaigns. 3. Strengthen public and institutional recognition of journalists’ rights and protection needs.
Outcomes: 1. Increased national awareness of press freedom and journalist safety issues during key UN days. 2. Stronger public and stakeholder engagement on access to information and accountability. 3. Enhanced visibility of challenges faced by journalists, contributing to pressure for safer working conditions.
Key Activities: • Organize public events, panel discussions, and media campaigns aligned with the three UN days. • Produce and disseminate targeted content (articles, social media, radio segments) highlighting each theme. • Engage journalists, media support organizations, and relevant stakeholders during these observances. • Monitor reach and impact of campaigns conducted around each UN day.
Deliverables: • Event reports for each UN day • Communication and media outputs • Progress report • Final report
Conclusion: By concentrating efforts around globally recognized UN observance days, this workplan takes a targeted, high-impact approach to strengthening freedom of expression and journalist safety in Afghanistan, and using visibility to drive awareness, engagement, and incremental change.
